picked.t: 호치민시, ‘베트남 문화의 날’ 도시 3곳서 불꽃놀이 개최…24일 밤9시부터 15분간
picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남 호치민시가 ‘베트남 문화의 날’을 기념해 오는 24일 밤 9시부터 도시 3곳에서 불꽃놀이 행사를 연다. 당국은 이 외 도시 곳곳에서 다양한 문화예술 행사를 개최할 계획이다. 호치민시 문화체육국이 최근 내놓은 ‘베트남 문화의 날 행사계획’에 따르면 오는 24일 밤 9시부터 15분간 △사이공동 응우옌후예 보행자거리 △투저우못동(phuong Thu Dau Mot) 사이공강변 박당공원(Bach Dang park) △붕따우동(phuong Vung Au) 8월광장탑 등 3곳에서 고공 불꽃놀이가 열릴 계획이다. 또한 행사장 3곳에서는 불꽃놀이 1시간 전 베트남 문화의 날을 기념하는 특별예술프로그램이 동시 진행될 예정이다. 이에 대해 응우옌 만 끄엉(Nguyen Manh Cuong) 호치민시 인민위원회 부위원장은 “이전 계획과 달리 옛 빈즈엉 지역의 불꽃놀이 행자장을 빈즈엉신도시중앙공원에서 박당공원으로 바꿨다. 새 장소는 사이공강변 박당 거리의 상징물 깐화저우(Canh hoa dau)와 인접해 강변 양쪽 투저우못동과 빈미사(xa Binh My) 지역민들이 넓은 공간에서 불꽃놀이를 즐길 수 있을 것”이라고 설명했다. 불꽃놀이 외에 21~24일에는 호치민시 인민위원회 청사앞과 렉스호텔 일대에서는 3D 맵핑 공연이 열린다. 이번 행사는 호치민시가 11월 초부터 12월 30일까지 168개 동·사·특구에서 여는 베트남 문화의 날 기념 행사 가운데 하나다. 이번 프로그램은 극장과 문화시설, 공공장소, 주거지, 학교, 공단 등 다양한 장소에서 진행된다. 주요 행사 중 하나는 18일부터 24일까지 진행될 응우옌후에 보행자거리에서 진행될 대단결-베트남 문화의 색’ 축제다. 본행사는 22일 오후 7시 개막하며 다양한 문화·예술·체육 활동과 교류·체험 행사로 호치민시의 문화 정체성을 지역민과 관광객에게 선보일 예정이다. 18~25일에는 문화·대단결 주간의 선전화와 예술 전시가 여러 곳에서 열리며, 개막식은 18일 오전 찌랑공원에서 예정돼 있다. 23일 밤에는 호조(Hozo) 2026 음악 축제의 시작을 알리는 공연이 사이공강변공원에서 열린다. 꼰다오(Con Dao)에서는 19~22일 '꼰다오 전설(Huyen thoai Con Dao)'을 주제로 한 도서전이 열린다. 도서·자료·사진 전시와 '휴먼 라이브러리' 토론회, 디지털 도서관 활동이 포함된다. 이 밖에도 호치민시는 레반땀공원과 응우옌반빈 책거리 등에서 국제 사진전을 열 예정이며, 호치민시 미술관과 람선공원에서는 '호치민시 미술전 - 창의 문화, 미래를 짓다' 전시행사가 예정돼 있다. 22~24일에는 응우옌후에 보행자거리 일대 영화, 공연예술, 소프트웨어·게임, 공예, 광고, 문화관광, 디지털 전환 등 대표 문화산업을 소개하는 공간이 마련된다. 전시와 체험을 결합해 관람객이 제품 제작 과정을 살펴보고, 전통 공예와 장인의 기법 시연을 보고, 직접 만들어 볼 수 있다. 가상현실과 증강현실 등 디지털 기술도 유산·문화상품·관광지 소개에 활용된다.

picked.t: Vietnam Connect Forum 2026 to connect FDI enterprises with business opportunities
picked.body: The half-day event, scheduled from 8:30 a.m. to noon at Vinpearl Landmark 81, Autograph Collection, will host discussions covering investment policies, tax regulations, economic trends and financial market developments. The agenda will also include pre-arranged business meetings connecting companies with potential service providers. Speakers will examine Vietnam's investment policies and business environment, including changes to corporate income tax, value-added tax and personal income tax, as well as tax administration, investment incentives and support policies. Other topics will include Vietnam's economic outlook, global developments, international trade, interest rates, foreign exchange movements and investment flows. The three speakers are Bui Thu Thuy, deputy director of the Foreign Investment Agency under the Ministry of Finance; Nguyen Thi Cuc, president of the Vietnam Tax Consultants' Association and former deputy director general of the General Department of , Ministry of Finance; and economist Nguyen Xuan Thanh. The forum will also feature a Business Matching program, with meetings arranged in advance based on participants' cooperation needs. The program will connect FDI enterprises with providers of logistics, legal advisory, investment consulting, accounting and finance, and general contracting services. Participants will be able to assess potential partners and explore services relevant to their operations and expansion plans. VietinBank said the forum is part of its efforts to support FDI enterprises beyond conventional banking services, using its domestic and international network to connect businesses with expertise and potential partners. The bank provides FDI clients with working capital financing, cash management, domestic and international payments, and trade finance. It also offers market and policy updates and connections with specialists and advisory organizations. Vietnam Connect Forum 2026 – Vietnam Investment and Business Networking Forum Date: Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026 Time: 8:30 a.m. - noon Venue: Vinpearl Landmark 81, Autograph Collection, 720A Dien Bien Phu Street, Vinhomes Tan Cang, Thanh My Tay Ward, Ho Chi Minh City Participants: FDI enterprises, investors, and domestic and international organizations Businesses interested in attending Vietnam Connect Forum 2026 or participating in Business Matching can register or submit their partnership requests directly at the nearest VietinBank branch or transaction office, or through the following channels: Email: fdi@vietinbank.vn Hotline: 1900 558 886

picked.t: Vietnam tourism website is 2nd busiest in Southeast Asia after Singapore
picked.body: VisitSingapore.com had nearly 424,000 visits, up 6%, according to digital analytics platform Similarweb. Thailand's Tourismthailand.org was third with around 338,000 visits, down 20% from the previous month. Vietnam.travel also recorded stronger visitor engagement than its regional counterparts, with visitors spending an average of 53 seconds on the website, compared with 44 seconds on Singapore's and 43 seconds on Thailand's portals. The Vietnamese website averaged 1.92 pages viewed per visit as against 1.63 for VisitSingapore.com and 1.76 for Tourismthailand.org. International visitors accounted for nearly 91% of Vietnam.travel's traffic, compared with 86% for Singapore and 62% for Thailand. The Vietnam National Authority of Tourism said Vietnam.travel is undergoing upgrades to its interface, content and technology to better support international visitors throughout their trips in the country. The website, which initially offered content only in English, now has 10 more languages: Japanese, Chinese, Korean, French, German, Russian, Spanish, Portuguese, Hindi, and Thai. It covers nature, culture, heritage, islands and coastal destinations, cuisine, leisure, and travel experiences. The platform is also being developed to incorporate services such as tour searches, flight bookings, hotel reservations, attraction tickets, transportation, eSIMs, and golf course access. Visitors will be able to choose services, submit booking requests, and make online payments through these integrated connections. Artificial intelligence is on the cards to support conversational translation, information searches, travel consultations, and personalized itinerary planning based on individual preferences. The authority aims to transform Vietnam.travel from a destination information website into a platform connecting international visitors with local destinations, domestic businesses, and service providers. The development is being carried out in phases, depending on progress in partner integration, data standardization, system testing, and service rollout.

picked.t: 베트남 부총리 “운송료, 휘발유 감세분 만큼 인하돼야” 지시…연말까지 물가관리 총력
picked.body: 호치민시의 한 주유소에서 오토바이에 주유 중인 시민. 응우옌 반 탕(Nguyen Van Thang) 베트남 부총리가 운송료 인하를 촉구하고 나섰다. 휘발유에 대한 세금을 낮춰준 만큼 각 운송 업체들의 운송비에도 세금 감면분이 반영되어야 한다는 취지다. 앞서 베트남 정부는 11월부터 내년 3월까지 휘발유에 대한 특별소비세율을 한시적으로 면제하는 한편, 전기요금 소매가를 평균 2% 인하한 바 있다. 정부는 해당 조치로 인해 올해 소비자물가지수(CPI)가 평균 4.5~4.7% 수준에 머물 것으로 기대하고 있다. 탕 부총리는 지난 9일 열린 물가관리운영위원회 회의에서 휘발유 특소세율 0%, 전기요금 평균 2% 인하 이후 투입 비용과 상품·서비스 가격 변동을 면밀히 모니터링할 것을 각 부처 및 기관, 지방자치단체에 지시했다. 공상부에는 감세 효과가 연료 판매가격에 적절히 반영되는지 감시하고, 수급을 살피며 가격을 운영하고 공급을 보장하는 과제가 주어졌다. 또한 건설부는 운송요금 신고·게시 실태 점검을 강화하고, 연료비가 내려가면 업체들로 하여금 요금을 이에 상응하게 낮추도록 요구해야 한다. 각 지자체 또한 관내 업체들의 가격 규정 준수 실태, 특히 생필품과 운송, 외식, 숙박 서비스에 맞춰 집중 점검에 나설 계획이다. 재무부에 따르면, 지난달 베트남의 CPI는 전월 대비 0.2% 상승했는데, 주로 국제 유가 상승에 따른 석유제품 가격 상승이 주범으로 지목됐다. 10월 기준 CPI는 평균 전년 동기 대비 4.57% 올랐고, 에너지·의료비·교육비 등 국가가 관리하는 품목과 가격변동성이 높은 식품을 제외한 근원 CPI는 4.24% 상승했다. 지역별로는 전국 34개 성·시 가운데 20개 지방의 CPI 상승률이 4.5%를 밑돌았다. 베트남중앙은행(SBV)와 재무부는 올해 CPI 상승률이 4.5~4.7% 범위에 머물 것으로 전망했다. 11~12월은 소비 수요 증가와 동시에 에너지 가격 변동, 식품 가격, 공공투자용 건축자재 수요가 물가에 상방 압력을 가할 것으로 예상되는 가운데, 정부는 한시적 휘발유 감세 및 전기료 인하 조치와 더불어 생필품 공급 보장 조치가 이러한 압력을 일부 상쇄할 것으로 기대하고 있다. 탕 부총리는 “국가가 관리하는 상품·서비스 가격은 올 연말까지 안정세를 유지해야 한다”며 정부 차원의 물가 관리의 중요성을 강조하며, 현재 시행 중인 각종 세금·수수료 면제·감면·연장 정책의 효과를 평가하고, 필요 시 국민과 기업을 지원하기 위한 내년도 지원 정책과 수준 검토를 각 부처 및 기관에 지시했다.

picked.t: Vietnamese hospital receives Japanese cell therapy technology for cancer and chronic disease treatment
picked.body: Vietnam's Tam Anh General Hospital Group and Japan's Grandsoul Medical Group have completed the transfer of natural killer (NK) immune cell and mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) technologies, marking a new step in medical cooperation between the two countries. Developed by the Grandsoul Research Institute for Immunology in Nara, Japan, two technologies being transferred to Tam Anh hospital are autologous NK therapy, and autologous MSC therapy. The first one includes the protocols of cell activation, expansion, evaluation and preparation for cancer treatment, while the second includes adipose tissue processing, cell isolation, expansion and evaluation. The completion of the technology transfer was announced on Nov. 9 during a visit to Japan by a high-level Vietnamese delegation from Nov. 8 to 11. The ceremony was witnessed by Party General Secretary and President To Lam and senior officials from both countries. Tam Anh is one of the first institutions in Vietnam selected, on an exclusive basis, for the comprehensive transfer of these core technologies from leading Japanese group Grandsoul. The transfer opens up new opportunities for treatment of cancer and chronic diseases and improving the health of people in Vietnam. Mastering cell therapy (stem cells and immune cells) to treat cancer, chronic diseases and intractable diseases is a national strategy approved by the Government for implementation from 2026 to 2030. This comprehensive, in-depth transfer is good news, as it makes this the first strategic technology realized ahead of schedule in Vietnam. According to Tam Anh , the technologies are intended for use across its five facilities in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi, which together handle more than 10,000 patient visits daily. NK cells are lymphocytes that belong to the innate immune system and act as rapid first-line defense against abnormal cells, including cancer cells. Under the transferred technology, immune cells are collected from a patient's blood, isolated and cultured under specialized conditions to increase their numbers and activate their functions before being infused back into the patient. NK cell-based therapies are being investigated for several cancers, including breast, lung, stomach, bladder, kidney and colorectal cancers. Their effectiveness and appropriate use, however, depend on the cancer type, treatment and available clinical evidence. Ta Thanh Van, chairman of the Professional Council of Tam Anh General Hospital for Regenerative Medicine and Cell Therapy in Hanoi, said NK cell therapy could provide an additional option alongside surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and targeted therapy. The second technology involves MSCs derived from a patient's own adipose tissue. The cells are isolated, processed and cultured before being prepared for use in the same patient. MSCs have been well-studied for their ability to regulate immune responses and support tissue repair. They have demonstrated therapeutic potential for cardiovascular and neurological conditions, including stroke and dementia, as well as diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and dermatological treatments. Many of these applications remain under clinical investigation, and their effectiveness and regulatory status vary by condition. Before the transfer, Japanese specialists visited Tam Anh to assess its facilities, laboratories and cell-processing procedures. The hospital said the assessment found that its infrastructure and processes met the technical requirements. Matsuo Yoshinobu, a senior technology specialist at the Grandsoul Nara Institute of Immunology Research, said Tam Anh had established the infrastructure, workforce and quality-control procedures needed to receive the technologies. "We are ready to work together to develop regenerative medicine in Vietnam safely, with treatment effectiveness and patient safety as our top priorities," he said. Van said the hospital had invested in specialized equipment, skilled personnel and international research partnerships to prepare for the transfer. Tam Anh established a tissue and umbilical cord blood bank, licensed by Vietnam's Ministry of Health in 2019 before developing its Center for Regenerative Medicine and Cell Therapy. The hospital has also invested in advanced diagnostic and treatment equipment, including CT and 3-Tesla MRI scanners, PET/CT imaging and molecular diagnostics. It operates two Da Vinci Xi robotic surgical systems and reports having performed more than 600 robotic procedures. Its cancer services include chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy and multidisciplinary treatment. A Mevion S250-FIT proton therapy system from the U.S., valued at nearly VND2 trillion (US$78.2 million), is being installed ahead of planned operation. According to Tam Anh, the technology transfer will help it develop domestic capabilities in cell isolation, cell culture and preparation under standards established by its Japanese partner. Ngo Chi Dung, chairman of Tam Anh Ge

picked.t: 베트남, ‘7월 27일 상이군인·열사의 날’ 공휴일 지정 추진…통과 시 내년부터 시행
picked.body: 지난달 호치민시에서 1968년 베트남전 당시 구정 대공세 당시 발굴된 전몰자 유해를 레 민 흥 베트남 총리(앞줄 오른쪽) 등 베트남 지도부가 운구 중인 모습.  (사진=베트남정부포털) 베트남 정부가 법개정을 통해 매년 7월 27일을 상이군인·순국열사의 날로 지정, 공휴일을 추가하는 방안을 추진하고 있다. 이번 노동법 개정안에는 11월 24일 베트남 문화의 날 역시 공휴일로 담겨 있어, 개정안이 통과되면 베트남의 연간 공휴일은 현재 11일에서  13일로 늘어날 전망이다. 9일 오전 베트남 국회는 노동법과 기록보존법, 양성평등법, 적십자활동법, 고용법의 일부개정·보완안을 심의했다. 이날 법안 설명에서 응우옌 띠엔 하이(Nguyen Tien Hai) 베트남 내무부 장관은 “노동법 개정안에 매년 7월 27일을 상이군인·열사의 날로 지정, 내년부터 법정공휴일로 시행하자는 제안을 받아들였다”고 설명했다. 그는 이어 “이번 공휴일 추가안은 국가유공자와 혁명유공자를 기리고, 근로자들로 하여금 보은하는 활동에 참여하고 민족의 아름다운 전통을 이어가도록 하려는 취지”라고 덧붙였다. 상이군인·열사의 날 외에도 개정안에는 정치국 결의안 제80호를 법제화하기 위해 11월 24일 베트남 문화의 날을 올해부터 법정공휴일로 지정한다는 내용이 담겼다. 현재 베트남의 공휴일은 연간 11일로, 여기에는 △신정 1일 △뗏(Tet 설) 5일 △훙왕기일(음력 3월 10일) 1일 △통일절(남부해방기념일, 4월 30일) 1일 △노동절(5월 1일) 1일 △국경절(9월 2일) 2일 등이 포함된다. 여기에 개정안을 통해 상이군인·열사의 날(2027년 시행)과 베트남 문화의 날(11월 24일)이 추가되면 내년부터 연간 공휴일은 13일로 늘어난다. 앞서 베트남 정부는 지난 2019년 노동법 개정 당시에도 7월 27일을 공휴일로 지정하는 방안을 추진한 바 있다. 정부는 당시 “상이군인·열사의 날은 문화적 상징이 됐고 민족의 보은 전통을 보여준다”며 “해외 여러 국가에서도 유사한 성격의 날을 공휴일로 지정하고 있어 국제적 관행과도 일치한다”고 설명했다. 그러나 해당 방안은 국회 문턱을 넘지 못했는데, 일부 의원들은 열사와 유공자에 대한 보은 활동이 정기적으로 이뤄지고 있는 점, 전몰자 유가족들의 슬픔을 되살리고 장기화할 수 있다는 점 등을 이유로 반대 의사를 피력했다.

picked.t: HCMC plans logistics hub network across 10 locations
picked.body: The 10 locations planned are Cat Lai, Long Binh, Linh Trung, Saigon Hi-Tech Park, Tan Kien, Hiep Phuoc, Cu Chi, Hoc Mon, Binh Khanh and the area around Tan Son Nhat International Airport. The plan is part of a resolution on free trade zones and integrated logistics zones approved by the municipal People's Council on Oct. 30. The network will connect industrial parks and production areas with ports, airports and markets. Goods will be consolidated, sorted, stored, processed and transferred at the hubs before reaching their destinations. The city expects the system to reduce unnecessary freight movements, lower transport costs and limit heavy truck traffic in densely populated areas. Following its merger with Binh Duong and Ba Ria-Vung Tau provinces, HCMC is home to an estimated 60-70% of Vietnam's logistics companies, according to the municipal administration. More than 15,300 businesses operate in logistics, transport, warehousing, bonded storage, seaport services and related sectors across the expanded city. However, the sector faces challenges involving operating costs, land use and infrastructure connectivity. Warehouses are scattered and often small, while large distribution centers and integrated logistics hubs remain limited. Freight transport relies heavily on roads, with inadequate connections among road, inland waterway, rail, seaport and air networks. Logistics costs account for an estimated 16-17% of Vietnam's GDP, while transportation makes up 50-70% of total logistics expenses, depending on the industry and transport mode. For seafood and agricultural products, logistics can represent 20-25% of total costs, affecting competitiveness. Demand for freight services is expected to rise as HCMC expands its industrial and transport infrastructure. The city's master plan provides for 105 export processing and industrial zones covering about 50,288 hectares. Major facilities, including the Cai Mep-Thi Vai port complex, the planned Can Gio International Transshipment Port, Tan Son Nhat International Airport and Long Thanh International Airport, are also expected to increase cargo volumes and demand for domestic and international freight services. The proposed hubs will integrate logistics functions, improve the use of transport infrastructure and reduce heavy freight traffic through urban areas. The city also plans to promote digital management, automation and environmentally sustainable logistics practices. Investment incentives for integrated logistics zones Under the resolution, HCMC will develop two types of integrated logistics zones: facilities within free trade zones and independent facilities outside them. The approval process, from consultation with relevant authorities to licensing, must not exceed 30 days. Investors developing infrastructure for these zones will be eligible for land rental exemptions and interest rate support from the municipal budget for up to seven years. Separately, HCMC plans to establish a free trade zone covering more than 4,165 hectares near Cai Mep Ha port. The zone will include logistics, industrial production, trade and services, education and training, research and development, digital technology facilities, data centers and non-tariff areas. The municipal administration said the free trade zone and integrated logistics zones would serve complementary roles. The former is intended to attract investment in manufacturing, trade, import-export activities and value-added services, while the latter will provide facilities for storing, processing, distributing and transferring goods across the city's transport network.

picked.t: Motion sickness fuels demand for long-distance motorbike taxis
picked.body: On Nov. 3, Ly Van Thanh, 24, traveled from Bac Ninh to Lao Cai Province to collect a female passenger heading to Hanoi. She paid more than VND2 million (US$80) for the 238-kilometer journey. "Every single day I get three to four booking requests, but I only take one to stay healthy and sharp," Thanh says. Thanh previously worked for app-based ride-hailing services, grinding 16 to 18 hours daily for meager returns of VND4,000 to VND5,000 per kilometer. In early 2026, realizing that severe motion sickness left many travelers eager to pay a premium for long-distance motorcycle travel across provinces, he walked away from the gig platforms to work for himself. He spent over VND10 million to upgrade his bike, outfitting it with high-traction tires, stronger shock absorbers, auxiliary headlights, heavy-duty cargo racks, and a custom-cushioned seat. In March, he took on his maiden private trip from the port city of Hai Phong to Hanoi. Along the route, he filmed his rides and shared them on social media. By May, a clip documenting a 200-kilometer run from Hai Phong to Quang Ninh racked up more than 350,000 views. From that point on, inquiries have been pouring in nonstop, and pushed his operational range to 400 to 500 kilometers across the rugged northern highlands. On a 412-kilometer haul once from Hai Phong to Son La, he rode straight between 7 p.m. to 6 a.m the next day. Every 100 kilometers, he made a point of stopping so that both he and his passenger could grab a bite and rest. "Early on, finishing a marathon haul like that would leave me knocked out for a day or two," he says. "Over time, my body adjusted; now I know my exact physical endurance limits and scout every route in detail before setting off." The business comes with some hazards, nevertheless. Once, he rode all the way from Hai Phong to Hanoi to pick up a traveler bound for the northwestern mountains, only to have the client cancel on arrival. In early September, he carried a passenger over 300 kilometers from Phu Tho up to Mu Cang Chai, and he only collected an advance of VND400,000. Having learned the hard way, he now has clear policies: clients must wire a 50% deposit upfront, no night trips or runs into deep wilderness with male passengers, and bookings are never subcontracted. "Clients book me because they trust my personal track record," he points out. "Passing clients off to a total stranger puts them in harm's way." Since pivoting fully into interprovincial motorcycle hires, Thanh has doubled or tripled the income he made on ride-hailing apps. Women struggling with acute motion sickness make up 95% of his clientele, and his personal social media channels have drawn 118,000 followers. Xuan Anh, 29, based in Ninh Binh Province has been offering the same service for the last three months, and also witnessed an explosion in long-haul demand. Xuan Anh charges VND8,000 per kilometer plus a VND3,000 surcharge per kilometer when picking up passengers in remote provinces. "The main advantage is keeping every dong without paying a cut to tech platforms," he says. "Clients willingly pay far more than conventional motorcycle taxis because the service is tailored, comfortable, and reliable." To handle demanding routes, Xuan Anh taught himself how to repair motorcycles, asks for a 70% deposit, and declines late-night trips with men. More than 80% of his clientele consists of women with motion sickness or people handling urgent business who need flexible, door-to-door transit. A smaller subset simply hires him to experience scenic, open-air motorcycle touring. The dread of motion sickness has turned long-distance motorcycle trips from the occasional one by drivers like Ly Van Thanh and Xuan Anh into a booming transport niche. Across social media feeds, dozens of independent drivers now advertise private, on-demand cross-country journeys. Examining the trend, economist Huynh Thanh Dien in Ho Chi Minh City notes that gig workers walking away from algorithmic platforms with their rigid pricing rules and policy constraints to cultivate personal brands and direct client followings represents a logical evolution in the freelance economy. "Still, this isn't a game everyone can play." Making a viable living out of this trade requires savvy self-marketing skills, an impeccable long-term reputation, cardiovascular stamina, a rock-solid vehicle, and quick instincts for dealing with roadside trouble. Looking ahead, both Thanh and Anh believe the market has enormous untapped potential as consumer appetite for personalized travel keeps expanding. But both point to an uncompromising golden rule for anyone wanting to jump in: respect every mile of the road, inspect your machine without cutting corners, and place rider and passenger safety above everything else. In mid-August, Nguyen Van Chi hired Thanh to drive her from Bac Ninh to her family home in Lao Cai. picked.t: Vietnamese single mother raises two children through travel and self-study
picked.body: At 6 a.m. on an early November morning, inside a mobile home parked in Son Tra Ward in Da Nang, Thi urged her daughter, Nhu Y, 14, to log into her online sewing class. While her daughter was in class, she phoned her son, Duy Thanh, to ask about his life in the dormitory of Vietnamese-German University in HCMC. In early September, he was admitted to the university’s electrical and computer engineering program on the strength of a GED certificate (equivalent to a U.S. high school diploma), an IELTS score of 7.5, and an SAT score of 1,390. These results came from Thanh’s five years of self-study. The family's nomadic life began following a tragedy in 2020. At the time, the HCMC native was working as an accountant while her husband was a bus driver. He was diagnosed with cancer and passed away within two months. Having lost her income after taking time off to care for her husband, she moved back to her mother's house with her two children, selling yogurt at the local market and crocheting to make ends meet. After his father's passing, Thanh, then 12 years old, became addicted to video games. Meanwhile, the memory of her husband's cancer made Thi pay greater attention to their living environment and food sources. She began researching in online communities of people who had left the city for the countryside By 2021, Thi sold her house and land, and moved her two children from HCMC to a house borrowed from a friend in Cu M’gar Commune in the central Dak Lak Province. Living alongside the Ede ethnic minority people, she noticed local children often accompanied their parents to the fields in the morning and attended school in the afternoon, yet remained healthy, had strong immune systems, and were helpful to others. This observation prompted her to redesign her children's education. Taking advantage of the shift to online schooling during the Covid-19 pandemic, she enrolled her two children in homeschooling under the United States’ Acellus program, which cost US$25 per month. All subjects were taught in English. To tackle her son's gaming addiction, she handed him a hoe to till the soil and clear weeds. She involved both children in tasks such as painting and repairing abandoned houses and building cabinets. Every day, Thanh went out with friends to play in the rain and splash around in streams, and helped tend fields of okra, scallions, cilantro, and radishes. Thanks to the increased outdoor physical activity, he spent significantly less time on his computer. Each month, she took her children to agricultural workshops where they learned to saw bamboo to build trellises for sponge gourds, prepare soil for growing vegetables, and study clean agriculture models, how biomass stoves work, and how to recycle biochar byproducts. To earn an income, Thi sold farm produce online and referred guests to homestays. Their nomadic life began when the family started relocating every three to six months, moving through places such as Hue, Da Nang, Binh Dinh Province, and Tuy An Nam Commune in Dak Lak Province. In mid-2023, while renting a home near the coast of Tuy An Nam, she sent Thanh to help out at Phuoc Luu’s coffee shop in Lo Village to gain real-world experience. Over three months, he waited tables, looked after the dogs, tended the garden, and learned how to make drinks. Outside of work hours, Thanh went swimming in the ocean with local children and studied on his computer in the evening. When Luu opened a community bookstore next to the coffee shop, Thanh helped clean, set up the premises, and plant vegetables and flowers with the younger kids. His strong English skills allowed him to serve foreign customers. He also joined trekking, camping, and waterfall expeditions, helping carry gear, cook meals, take photos, and support others. "The boy completely changed after that summer, becoming proactive, lively, and outgoing," Luu says. To make moving easier, in early 2025, Thi purchased and renovated an old mobile home for VND800 million. The shower area was downsized to make room for a kitchen cabinet and a washing machine. Inside this vehicle, Nhu Y has a dedicated corner for sewing, embroidery, and playing the violin. Both her children are now in charge of their own study schedules. Thi only monitors the schedules and uses an app to track the total hours they study each day.. "There is no single best educational environment for everyone, only an environment that fits each child," Thi says about her family's five-year journey.

picked.t: 베트남, 올해 ‘디지털경제’ 성장률 동남아 최고 전망…490억 달러 전년比 20%↑
picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 올해 베트남의 디지털 경제 규모가 490억 달러에 육박, 동남아에서 가장 빠른 성장세를 보일 것이란 전망이 나왔다. 구글·테마섹·베인&컴퍼니가 공동 조사해 발표한 ‘2026년 동남아 디지털경제 보고서(e-Conomy SEA 2026)'에 따르면, 올해 베트남의 디지털 경제는 주요 부문 전반에 걸쳐 두 자릿수 성장세를 유지, 시장 규모는 GMV(총상품거래액) 기준 490억 달러에 달할 것으로 전망됐다. 이는 지난해보다 20% 증가한 수준으로, 베트남은 말레이시아와 함께 동남아에서 가장 빠른 디지털 경제 성장세를 보일 것으로 예상된다. 부문별로는 전자상거래 부문의 GMV가 320억 달러로 전년 대비 22% 늘어 전체 베트남 디지털 경제의 약 3분의 2 비중을 차지할 것으로 전망됐다. 베트남 이커머스 시장은 올해 동남아에서 가장 빠른 성장세를 기록, 2030년 시장 규모는 610억 달러까지 확대될 것으로 전망된다. 다음으로는 온라인 미디어가 17% 증가한 70억 달러, 차량호출 및 음식배달 서비스가 60억 달러, 온라인 여행이 50억 달러로 각각 17%, 15% 늘 것으로 예상된다. 디지털 금융 또한 인상적인 확장세를 보이고 있다. 디지털 대출잔액은 34% 늘어 140억 달러에 달할 것으로 전망됐는데, 이는 베트남 디지털 경제 부문과 동남아 전체를 통틀어 가장 빠른 증가율이다. 디지털 결제액은 올해 1,970억 달러로 21% 늘고 2030년에는 3,020억 달러에 이를 전망이다. 올해 초만 해도 비현금 결제는 38% 증가율을 나타냈다. 생성형 인공지능(AI)은 소비자의 쇼핑과 여행 계획에 점점 더 쓰이고 있다. 베트남의 생성형 AI 이용자는 약 4,500만 명으로 노동력의 65%에 해당하며, 일상적 이용 정도는 동남아 1위다. 이용자 5명 중 2명이 매일 이 기술을 쓰고, 이용자 한 명은 평균 5개 이상의 AI 도구를 이용해 연간 310억 건의 질의를 만든다. 한편 인공지능(AI)은 베트남 쇼핑 및 여행 분야에서 입지를 확대하고 있다. 보고서에 따르면, 베트남의 생성형 AI 이용자는 전체 노동 인구의 65%인 4,500만 명으로 동남아 중 일일 AI 활용도가 가장 높은 것으로 나타났다. 특히 이용자 5명 중 2명은 생성형 AI를 일상적으로 쓰고 있으며, 이용자 1명은 평균 5개 이상의 AI 툴을 활용하고 있었다. 또한 베트남의 연간 AI 질의 건수는 총 310억 건에 달하는 것으로 조사됐다. AI는 베트남 소비 여정의 44%에서 시작점이 되고, 이용자 5명 중 4명이 쇼핑 업무를 AI 에이전트에 맡길 의향이 있다. 동남아 전체로는 특화 생성형 AI 플랫폼이 여행 계획의 두 번째로 인기 있는 출발점이 되어 소셜미디어를 앞질렀다. 베트남에서는 AI 대화의 80%가 베트남어로 이뤄져, 동남아 6대 디지털경제 가운데 가장 높다. 특히 베트남에서 소비자 여정의 44%는 AI에서 시작되며, 이용자 5명 중 4명은 쇼핑 관련 업무를 AI에이전트에 맡길 의향이 있는 것으로 조사됐다. 동남아 전체로 보면, 생성형 AI 플랫폼은 여행 계획을 시작하는 수단으로 소셜미디어(SNS)를 제치고 두 번째로 인기 있는 플랫폼으로 확고히 자리매김했다. 또한 베트남 내 AI 대화 사용자의 계정 80%는 베트남 사용자가 차지하는 등 베트남은 동남아 6대 디지털 경제국 가운데 AI 대화 비중이 가장 높은 것으로 조사됐다. 마크 우(Marc Woo) 구글베트남 대표는 “AI 중심 소비자 여정과 쇼핑 업무를 AI에이전트에게 맡기려는 이용자 의향에 대한 조사 결과는 해당 기술이 경제 성장을 이끌 잠재력을 보여주는 것”이라며 “특히 이커머스 플랫폼들은 고객 접근과 구매 전환율 제고, 상품 등록 등 판매자 업무 자동화를 위해 AI를 서비스에 통합하고 있다”고 설명했다.
